title: The Unspoken Key To Consistency
author: Michael Linsin
summary: Opening with a Rosa Parks quotation, Linsin argues that mental toughness, not a specific tactic, is the missing key to true, every-single-time consistency. He describes this internal fortitude as something possessed rather than applied, and addresses teachers who feel they lack it, worn down by fear of student or parent pushback. His prescribed solution is a perspective shift: teachers must reconnect with the larger purpose of their work, an idea he attributes to performance coach Brendon Burchard's concept of 'raising your necessity.' Remembering one's deeper 'why,' he argues, transforms consistency from an aspiration into an obligation, supplying the courage needed to defend the classroom management plan without wavering.

quotes: Knowing what must be done does away with fear.” -Rosa Parks
It isn’t something you apply or put into practice. It’s something you possess, on the inside.
It’s intestinal fortitude. It’s moxie, chutzpah, tenacity, grit, mettle.
There is only one way to acquire the internal strength that will enable you to be the confident, consistent leader your students can count on. You must change your perspective.

Remembering that you are part of something bigger than yourself is what Brendon Burchard, a high performance coach who works with CEOs, athletes, and entertainers like Usher and Oprah, calls “raising your necessity.
It becomes not just something you should do or want to do or wish you did. It becomes something you must do, need to do, have to do.
